headline: New top-level domains open for application in 2026, first time since 2012
summary: ICANN is opening a rare window for anyone to invent and apply for new internet domain extensions like .app or .shop, a process that last occurred over a decade ago.
details: For the first time since 2012, the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) will open applications for new top-level domains (TLDs) in 2026. This rare opportunity allows entities to create custom domain extensions like .app or .shop, with the application window closing on August 12.

ICANN, the global governance body for domain names and IP addresses, maintains the internet's stability and security without policing content. This principle was evident when ICANN declined Ukraine's request to shut down Russian TLDs in 2022.

The current ICANN86 meeting in Seville, Spain, is crucial as it's the last in-person gathering before the new TLD application window closes. Attendees include representatives from big tech, domain registrars, UN agencies, and government officials.

Owning a TLD allows a registry to sell domains through registrars for annual fees. Google famously paid $25 million for the .app string in 2012, generating significant revenue from yearly registrations.

Companies like Verisign, which operates .com, earn over a billion dollars annually from domain renewals, boasting 100% uptime for 28 years. The limited application window fuels significant FOMO among potential applicants, who remain secretive about their desired 'strings' until the public list is released on October 7.

headline: Xbox Elite Controller 3 specs leak via Xbox's own Design Lab backend
summary: The rumored controller, codenamed Edessa, may feature Hall-effect/TMR joysticks for drift-free play and advanced voice-coil haptics, similar to the PS5 DualSense.
details: Major features for the unannounced Xbox Elite Controller 3 have reportedly leaked directly from Microsoft's Xbox Design Lab backend. The leak suggests the controller, codenamed Edessa, will offer Hall-effect and TMR sticks, advanced haptics, and a dedicated audio scroll wheel.

Redditor u/esketitethan uncovered these details by examining configuration records and 3D component models within the Design Lab's system. The controller is linked to an accessory/customization product called Beatrice.

Unlike the Elite Series 2's potentiometer analog sticks prone to drift, the Elite Controller 3 is expected to use magnetic sensing technology. Its haptics are also upgraded to voice-coil haptics (VCAs) for more nuanced trigger vibration, similar to the PS5 DualSense.

Additional rumored features include performance D-pads with multiple choices, various faceplate options, low-friction/silent sticks, and new paddle designs. The leak also hints at four SKU combinations, including 'Elite Complete' and 'Elite Base' versions.

However, the original source files for this leak appear to have been removed, so take the information with caution. Some users are skeptical about Microsoft developing its own Hall-effect joysticks, while others note the continued absence of a built-in gyro.
